papers.title_zh: 本科生、清洁人员和保安人员对与狗相关的人畜共患疾病的知识、态度和做法
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Zoonotic diseases are a major public health challenge in Ethiopia, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas where human-animal interaction is high. Dogs are the primary transmitters of several critical diseases, such as rabies, echinococcosis, and leishmaniasis. Despite these risks, there is limited research on the awareness levels of high-risk groups within academic settings. This study aims to bridge this gap by assessing the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding dog-associated zoonotic diseases among undergraduate health students, cleaning staff, and security personnel. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted from April to June 2025, recruiting 424 participants through stratified random sampling with proportional allocation. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire administered via face-to-face interviews and an online Kobo Toolbox link to assess participants’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices. The data were entered into Excel and analyzed using SPSS version 27, with results presented in tables and narrative summaries; chi-square (χ2) tests were used to assess associations, and p-values less than 0.05 were considered statistically significant. Result Among the 424 respondents, 91.7% (n = 389) were aged 18–29 years, with 48.6% (n = 206) females and 51.4% (n = 216) males; most had college/university education (92.0%, n = 390). The majority were undergraduate health students (90.1%, n = 382), followed by security personnel (6.6%, n = 28) and cleaning workers (3.3%, n = 14). Most respondents had heard of zoonosis (91.5%, n = 388), recognized animal-to-human disease transmission (96.2%, n = 408), identified viruses (32.1%, n = 136) and believed that dogs pose community risks (82.3%, n = 349) and are sources of parasitic infections (84.9%, n = 360). Conclusion The most participants demonstrated good awareness and positive attitudes toward dog-associated zoonotic diseases. However, gaps in knowledge among some respondents highlight the need for targeted education to promote safer human–animal interactions.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 人畜共患疾病是埃塞俄比亚面临的主要公共卫生挑战,特别是在人与动物互动频繁的农村和城乡结合部地区。狗是多种严重疾病的主要传播者,例如 狂犬病、包虫病和利什曼病。尽管存在这些风险,但学术界对高风险群体的认识水平的研究仍然有限。本研究旨在通过评估本科生、清洁人员和保安人员对与狗相关的人畜共患疾病的知识、态度和实践来弥补这一差距。方法于2025年4月至6月进行横断面研究,采用分层随机抽样、按比例分配的方式招募424名参与者。使用半结构化问卷收集数据,该问卷通过面对面访谈和在线 Kobo Toolbox 链接进行管理,以评估参与者的知识、态度和实践。将数据输入 Excel 并使用 SPSS 27 版进行分析,结果以表格和叙述性摘要的形式呈现;卡方 (χ2) 检验用于评估关联性,p 值小于 0.05 被认为具有统计显着性。结果 424 名受访者中,91.7%(n = 389)年龄在 18-29 岁,其中女性占 48.6%(n = 206),男性占 51.4%(n = 216);大多数人受过大学教育(92.0%,n = 390)。大多数是卫生本科生(90.1%,n = 382),其次是保安人员(6.6%,n = 28)和清洁工人(3.3%,n = 14)。大多数受访者听说过人兽共患病(91.5%,n = 388),认识到动物传染人类的疾病传播(96.2%,n = 408),识别出病毒(32.1%,n = 136),并认为狗会带来社区风险(82.3%,n = 349)并且是寄生虫感染的来源(84.9%,n = 360)。结论 大多数参与者对犬类人畜共患疾病表现出良好的认识和积极的态度。然而,一些受访者之间的知识差距凸显了有针对性的教育的必要性,以促进更安全的人与动物互动。

papers.full_text: Nature Reviews Microbiology nature reviews microbiology https://doi.org/10.1038/s41579-026-01372-1 Review article Check for updates Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses Hendrik Jan Thibaut 1, Dirk Jochmans 1,3, Christophe Van Dijck2,3, Manon Laporte 1,3, Laurens Liesenborghs 2 & Johan Neyts1 Abstract Small molecule antiviral drugs have transformed the management of infections such as those caused by HIV, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, herpesviruses and influenza viruses. Effective antiviral therapeutics remain unavailable for many other often life-threatening viral infections, many of which are caused by RNA viruses. The development of potent, safe and orally available antivirals is therefore essential both to address current unmet medical needs and to strengthen epidemic and pandemic preparedness. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for building a diversified portfolio of broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses with activity spanning multiple genera, entire families or even crossing viral families. We provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses and discuss the biological determinants that underlie their antiviral spectrum. Finally, we outline the clinical development frameworks required to accelerate the evaluation of such drugs, in particular in the context of outbreaks. Sections Introduction One drug to treat them all? Direct-acting antivirals versus host-targeting antivirals New approaches to discover new targets for broader-acting antivirals Translational readiness Conclusions 1KU Leuven Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Transplantation, Antiviral Drug and Vaccine Research Group, Leuven, Belgium. 2Department of Clinical Sciences, Institute of Tropical Medicine, Antwerp, Belgium. 3These authors contributed equally: Dirk Jochmans, Christophe Van Dijck, Manon Laporte. e-mail: johan.neyts@kuleuven.be Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article Alongside vaccine development, sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery is therefore essential. Antiviral drug development has so far largely been focused on viral infections that offer large and predict- able commercial markets (for example, those caused by HIV and HCV). It is obviously unrealistic and economically unsustainable to develop specific antiviral drugs for each known viral pathogen. Newly emerging viruses will most likely belong to viral families already known (Table 1) today. Advances in metagenomics and high-throughput sequencing greatly expanded our understanding of viral diversity, and although new viral families may still be discovered, such events are becoming increasingly rare. Together, this strongly supports a strategy in which broader-acting small molecule antiviral (BSA) drugs are developed. Such drugs can be used for the treatment and prophylaxis of infec- tions with known viruses for which no antiviral treatment is available and, in the case of epidemics or pandemics, as a rapid response option while other countermeasures, such as vaccines and mAbs, are being developed12,13. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for the development of BSAs and provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved or experi- mental antiviral drugs active against viruses with an RNA genome. We also outline strategies for target discovery and accelerated clinical development. One drug to treat them all? The term ‘broad-spectrum’ antiviral has been widely used but lacks, to the best of our knowledge, a clear definition. Here, we propose instead to use the term ‘broader-spectrum’ antivirals and distinguish three categories: (i) cross-family BSAs with activity across unrelated viral families within or across a certain genome architecture, that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA); (ii) pan-family BSAs that act across the different genera of a given viral family (for example, pan-paramyxovirus drugs); and (iii) intra-family BSAs, which are active against multiple serotypes and genotypes of a particular virus (for example, pan-serotype dengue virus (DENV) Introduction Viruses, whether known or yet to emerge (‘virus X’), remain a major threat to global health. Vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and antiviral drugs are each important and complementary in controlling viral infections. Vaccination has led to the eradication of smallpox, brought polio close to eradication and massively reduced disease and mortality associated with numerous viral infections, such as measles virus, mumps virus, rubella virus, influenza virus, severe acute respira- tory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human papillomavirus1–3. For several important human pathogens, such as HIV, hepatitis C virus (HCV), herpes simplex viruses (HSV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), rhinoviruses and many others, the devel- opment of highly effective vaccines has proved difficult or remains elusive, often despite decades of intensive effort. Therefore, it cannot be guaranteed that efficacious vaccines can always be developed when new threatening viruses emerge4,5. mAbs can offer immediate protection and are transforming the prophylaxis or treatment of certain acute viral diseases, such as those caused by the rabies virus6 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)7. They generally have an excellent safety profile and can be highly effective, although they require injections, are virus specific or variant spe- cific and can rapidly select for escape variants8,9. Like vaccines, mAbs can be developed only once a new pathogen has been identified and characterized. By contrast, small molecule antiviral drugs offer several distinct advantages. They can be administered orally and have the potential to cover a broader spectrum of viruses (Box 1) than vaccines and mAbs. Antiviral drugs have revolutionized the treatment of certain (chronic) viral infections such as those caused by either HIV, HBV, HCV, HSV-1 and HSV-2, and CMV. More recently, antiviral drugs have also become availa- ble against some other viruses including influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2 and hepatitis delta virus. However, for the majority of the more than 200 known human pathogenic viruses, no antiviral drugs are available. Most of these viruses are RNA viruses — the focus of this Review — including many emerging and clinically important pathogens10–12. Box 1 | Categories and examples of broader-spectrum antivirals (BSAs) for RNA viruses Cross-family BSAs Active against viruses belonging to different (related or unrelated) viral families or across a certain genome architecture (that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA viruses)), typically by targeting conserved features of the viral replication machinery such as the catalytic site of viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases. For example, remdesivir, a nucleoside viral polymerase inhibitor, is active against viruses belonging to different viral families, that is, the (−)ssRNA Filoviridae, Paramyxoviridae, Pneumoviridae and Arenaviridae as well as the (+) ssRNA Flaviviridae, Picornaviridae and Coronaviridae. Baloxavir, an endonuclease inhibitor, inhibits influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae) but also, although much less potently, several members of the family Peribunyaviridae. Pan-family BSAs Active across all or at least most genera within a single viral family. Examples include neuraminidase inhibitors such as oseltamivir, zanamivir and peramivir that are active against both influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae). Nirmatrelvir is a reversible covalent, peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor that inhibits human and animal coronaviruses belonging to different genera within the family Coronaviridae. Intra-family BSAs Can be active against multiple serotypes, genotypes or strains of a particular virus species. For example, mosnodenvir is active against all dengue virus genotypes (family Flaviviridae) by blocking the interaction between viral proteins NS4B and NS3. Intra-family broader-spectrum activity may span several viruses within one genus of a particular family without extending to other genera. For example, the non-covalent, non-peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor ensitrelvir is active only against members of the genus Betacoronavirus (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), SARS-CoV-1 and human coronavirus (HCoV)-OC43), but not against members of the genus Alphacoronavirus (such as HCoV-229E and HCoV-NL63) within the family Coronaviridae. Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article inhibitors) or active against one or more (but not all) genera of a viral family (Box 1). The need for broader-acting antivirals and their desired spectrum of activity are mostly defined by the particular (clinical) context (Boxes 2 and 3). For viruses that cause a high number of annual cases (for example, RSV), there might be a sufficiently large market, and thus incentives, to develop virus-specific drugs. Conversely, there might be no or less financial incentive to develop virus-specific drugs for viruses that cause a rather limited number of cases but that col- lectively, within their genus or family, are responsible for a substan- tial clinical burden (for example, coxsackieviruses and echoviruses, EV-D68 and EV-A71 that all belong to the genus Enterovirus). In this case, the development of antivirals that are broadly active across the entire Enterovirus genus (pan-Enterovirus; category intra-family BSAs) represents a more realistic approach. In the context of epidemic or pan- demic preparedness, access to pan-family and cross-family BSAs may be particularly important, as it cannot be predicted which viral family a newly emerging pathogen (‘virus X’) will belong to. Given the extensive genetic diversity and distinct replication strategies of viral families, the development of a single cross-family drug with potent activity against all RNA virus families is likely to be unrealistic. Rather, a more feasible strategy may be to establish a portfolio of different types of BSAs that collectively provide, either alone or in combination, coverage across the RNA virus landscape. BSAs may also be valuable in the context of viral co-infections, in which a single drug could simultaneously target two (or more) viruses14,15. Beyond the spectrum of activity, BSA development must be guided by clearly defined target product profiles16. To have a meaningful clinical impact, BSAs (or combinations thereof) should ideally be highly efficacious, be orally available (preferably once daily dosing), be safe for a broad patient population (preferably including pregnant women and children), possess a (relatively) high barrier to resistance and exhibit minimal drug–drug interactions16. Virus tissue tropism further influences desirable drug properties. For example, infections involving the central nervous system require efficient blood–brain barrier penetration, whereas limited penetration may be preferable for peripheral viral infections. Consequently, distinct target product profiles may be required, even within a single viral genus. The importance of preparedness against known viruses (such as EV-D6818, Ebola virus19, monkeypox virus20 and Andes hantavirus21) as well as against emerging viral threats (for example, SARS-CoV-2) has been repeatedly illustrated during outbreaks caused by these diverse viral pathogens. During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19 pan- demic), no antiviral drugs were available at the onset. A stockpile of an oral, pan-family coronavirus BSA before the start of the COVID-19 pan- demic would likely have saved countless lives22,23. Remdesivir, originally discovered as an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) inhibitor of RSV24 and Ebola viruses25,26, was the only drug for which antiviral activity against coronaviruses had been systematically demonstrated in preclinical models before the pandemic27. In the absence of readily available and effective antiviral treat- ments, drug repurposing may need to be considered. Repurpos- ing can provide a rapid and relatively cost-effective response by leveraging de-risked drugs with existing preclinical and clinical safety data28,29. However, drugs developed or used for non-viral indi- cations are mostly unlikely to possess sufficient antiviral potency to curb outbreaks caused by newly emerging and (potentially highly) pathogenic viruses. At the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, extensive repurposing initiatives studied whether drugs approved for other indications could inhibit SARS-CoV-2 replication. Drugs such as azithro- mycin (antibiotic), itraconazole (antifungal), hydroxychloroquine (antimalarial, antirheumatic), niclosamide (anthelmintic), ivermectin (anthelmintic) and nitazoxanide (antiparasitic) rapidly entered numer- ous clinical trials, many of them small and underpowered, and even became, for some time, standard treatment in certain settings despite limited preclinical evidence30. Overall, drug repurposing efforts dur- ing the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic were largely unsuccessful, highlighting that such strategies should not be initiated only at the time a new virus emerges. A more realistic approach is to systematically assess existing drugs during epidemic or pandemic ‘peace-time’ against panels of viruses that are representative of high-risk families. Drugs with ‘reason- able’ in vitro activity can be further tested, alone or in combinations, in preclinical models13. Studies in SARS-CoV-2-infected hamsters revealed that combi- nations of two or three antivirals, each used at suboptimal or even inactive doses, can result in important antiviral effects31. To ration- ally develop combination strategies for BSAs, systematic preclinical testing of combinations across viral families is required. Extensive preclinical studies of the most promising combinations may help to guide strategies for stockpiling for epidemic or pandemic prepared- ness. The use of fixed-dose combinations (such as those used in the treatment of HIV infections) would be ideal. Yet, in outbreak situation with new pathogens, there will be insufficient time to develop such fixed-dose combinations; co-administration of individual drugs would therefore represent a more practical approach. full_text_sections.full_text: Nature Reviews Microbiology nature reviews microbiology https://doi.org/10.1038/s41579-026-01372-1 Review article Check for updates Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses Hendrik Jan Thibaut 1, Dirk Jochmans 1,3, Christophe Van Dijck2,3, Manon Laporte 1,3, Laurens Liesenborghs 2 & Johan Neyts1 Abstract Small molecule antiviral drugs have transformed the management of infections such as those caused by HIV, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, herpesviruses and influenza viruses. Effective antiviral therapeutics remain unavailable for many other often life-threatening viral infections, many of which are caused by RNA viruses. The development of potent, safe and orally available antivirals is therefore essential both to address current unmet medical needs and to strengthen epidemic and pandemic preparedness. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for building a diversified portfolio of broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses with activity spanning multiple genera, entire families or even crossing viral families. We provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses and discuss the biological determinants that underlie their antiviral spectrum. Finally, we outline the clinical development frameworks required to accelerate the evaluation of such drugs, in particular in the context of outbreaks. Sections Introduction One drug to treat them all? Direct-acting antivirals versus host-targeting antivirals New approaches to discover new targets for broader-acting antivirals Translational readiness Conclusions 1KU Leuven Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Transplantation, Antiviral Drug and Vaccine Research Group, Leuven, Belgium. 2Department of Clinical Sciences, Institute of Tropical Medicine, Antwerp, Belgium. 3These authors contributed equally: Dirk Jochmans, Christophe Van Dijck, Manon Laporte. e-mail: johan.neyts@kuleuven.be Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article Alongside vaccine development, sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery is therefore essential. Antiviral drug development has so far largely been focused on viral infections that offer large and predict- able commercial markets (for example, those caused by HIV and HCV). It is obviously unrealistic and economically unsustainable to develop specific antiviral drugs for each known viral pathogen. Newly emerging viruses will most likely belong to viral families already known (Table 1) today. Advances in metagenomics and high-throughput sequencing greatly expanded our understanding of viral diversity, and although new viral families may still be discovered, such events are becoming increasingly rare. Together, this strongly supports a strategy in which broader-acting small molecule antiviral (BSA) drugs are developed. Such drugs can be used for the treatment and prophylaxis of infec- tions with known viruses for which no antiviral treatment is available and, in the case of epidemics or pandemics, as a rapid response option while other countermeasures, such as vaccines and mAbs, are being developed12,13. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for the development of BSAs and provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved or experi- mental antiviral drugs active against viruses with an RNA genome. We also outline strategies for target discovery and accelerated clinical development. One drug to treat them all? The term ‘broad-spectrum’ antiviral has been widely used but lacks, to the best of our knowledge, a clear definition. Here, we propose instead to use the term ‘broader-spectrum’ antivirals and distinguish three categories: (i) cross-family BSAs with activity across unrelated viral families within or across a certain genome architecture, that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA); (ii) pan-family BSAs that act across the different genera of a given viral family (for example, pan-paramyxovirus drugs); and (iii) intra-family BSAs, which are active against multiple serotypes and genotypes of a particular virus (for example, pan-serotype dengue virus (DENV) Introduction Viruses, whether known or yet to emerge (‘virus X’), remain a major threat to global health. Vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and antiviral drugs are each important and complementary in controlling viral infections. Vaccination has led to the eradication of smallpox, brought polio close to eradication and massively reduced disease and mortality associated with numerous viral infections, such as measles virus, mumps virus, rubella virus, influenza virus, severe acute respira- tory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human papillomavirus1–3. For several important human pathogens, such as HIV, hepatitis C virus (HCV), herpes simplex viruses (HSV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), rhinoviruses and many others, the devel- opment of highly effective vaccines has proved difficult or remains elusive, often despite decades of intensive effort. Therefore, it cannot be guaranteed that efficacious vaccines can always be developed when new threatening viruses emerge4,5. mAbs can offer immediate protection and are transforming the prophylaxis or treatment of certain acute viral diseases, such as those caused by the rabies virus6 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)7. They generally have an excellent safety profile and can be highly effective, although they require injections, are virus specific or variant spe- cific and can rapidly select for escape variants8,9. Like vaccines, mAbs can be developed only once a new pathogen has been identified and characterized. By contrast, small molecule antiviral drugs offer several distinct advantages. They can be administered orally and have the potential to cover a broader spectrum of viruses (Box 1) than vaccines and mAbs. Antiviral drugs have revolutionized the treatment of certain (chronic) viral infections such as those caused by either HIV, HBV, HCV, HSV-1 and HSV-2, and CMV. More recently, antiviral drugs have also become availa- ble against some other viruses including influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2 and hepatitis delta virus. However, for the majority of the more than 200 known human pathogenic viruses, no antiviral drugs are available. Most of these viruses are RNA viruses — the focus of this Review — including many emerging and clinically important pathogens10–12. Box 1 | Categories and examples of broader-spectrum antivirals (BSAs) for RNA viruses Cross-family BSAs Active against viruses belonging to different (related or unrelated) viral families or across a certain genome architecture (that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA viruses)), typically by targeting conserved features of the viral replication machinery such as the catalytic site of viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases. For example, remdesivir, a nucleoside viral polymerase inhibitor, is active against viruses belonging to different viral families, that is, the (−)ssRNA Filoviridae, Paramyxoviridae, Pneumoviridae and Arenaviridae as well as the (+) ssRNA Flaviviridae, Picornaviridae and Coronaviridae. Baloxavir, an endonuclease inhibitor, inhibits influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae) but also, although much less potently, several members of the family Peribunyaviridae. Pan-family BSAs Active across all or at least most genera within a single viral family. Examples include neuraminidase inhibitors such as oseltamivir, zanamivir and peramivir that are active against both influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae). Nirmatrelvir is a reversible covalent, peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor that inhibits human and animal coronaviruses belonging to different genera within the family Coronaviridae. papers.title_original: Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease. It addresses the development of broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals (BSAs) against RNA viruses, including rabies virus, with the aim of creating antivirals that can target multiple genera, families, or even cross families. The central question is whether such broad-spectrum antivirals can be developed and used effectively for rabies and other RNA viruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of antiviral agents active against RNA viruses, including rabies virus. It discusses the rationale for developing BSAs, provides an overview of approved and experimental antivirals, and outlines the biological determinants and clinical development frameworks for these drugs. The review does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria, but it is based on a comprehensive examination of the literature.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the development of broader-spectrum antivirals is essential to address current unmet medical needs and to strengthen epidemic and pandemic preparedness. It highlights that rabies virus, along with other RNA viruses, is a priority for such antiviral development due to its pandemic potential and broad host range. The review also emphasizes the importance of fixed-dose combinations for treating infections caused by RNA viruses.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that some antivirals, such as azithromycin, itraconazole, and hydroxychloroquine, were rapidly tested in clinical trials with limited preclinical evidence, raising concerns about their efficacy and safety. Additionally, the review highlights that the term 'broad-spectrum' antiviral lacks a clear definition, and there is a need for more precise terminology and criteria. There is also a gap in understanding the mechanisms that underlie the antiviral spectrum of these drugs.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that research should focus on developing potent, safe, and orally available antivirals for rabies and other RNA viruses. It also recommends that clinical development frameworks be accelerated, particularly for outbreaks, and that fixed-dose combinations be explored for the treatment of RNA virus infections. Furthermore, it emphasizes the importance of sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery to address both known and emerging viral threats.

analysis.summary_en: This review discusses the development of broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals (BSAs) against RNA viruses, including rabies virus. It highlights the need for such drugs to address current unmet medical needs and improve pandemic preparedness. The review outlines the rationale for BSAs, provides an overview of existing and experimental antivirals, and emphasizes the importance of fixed-dose combinations. It also notes controversies around the use of certain antivirals with limited evidence and identifies gaps in understanding the mechanisms of antiviral activity. The implications suggest that research should prioritize the development of potent, safe, and orally available antivirals for rabies and other RNA viruses, with accelerated clinical frameworks for outbreaks.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病。它解决了针对RNA病毒(包括狂犬病病毒)的更广谱直接作用抗病毒药物(BSA)的开发,旨在创建可以针对多个属、科甚至跨科的抗病毒药物。核心问题是这样的广谱抗病毒药物是否可以开发并有效用于狂犬病和其他RNA病毒。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 抗病毒药物 活性抗 RNA 病毒药物(包括 狂犬病病毒)的系统分析。它讨论了开发 BSA 的基本原理,概述了已批准和实验性的 抗病毒药物,并概述了这些药物的生物决定因素和临床开发框架。该综述没有明确报告数据库、检索日期或资格标准,但它是基于对文献的全面审查。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,开发更广谱的 抗病毒药物 对于解决当前未满足的医疗需求和加强流行病和大流行的防范至关重要。它强调,狂犬病病毒 与其他 RNA 病毒一样,由于其大流行潜力和广泛的 宿主 范围,是 抗病毒药物 开发的优先事项。该综述还强调了固定剂量组合治疗 RNA 病毒引起的感染的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,一些 抗病毒药物,如阿奇霉素、伊曲康唑和羟氯喹,在临床前证据有限的情况下迅速进行了临床试验,引发了对其有效性和安全性的担忧。此外,审查还强调,“广谱”抗病毒药物 一词缺乏明确的定义,需要更精确的术语和标准。对这些药物 抗病毒药物 谱背后的机制的理解也存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查建议研究应集中于开发针对 狂犬病 和其他 RNA 病毒的有效、安全且口服的 抗病毒药物。它还建议加快临床开发框架,特别是暴发,并探索针对RNA病毒感染的治疗的固定剂量组合。此外,它还强调了持续投资 抗病毒药物 药物发现以应对已知和新出现的病毒威胁的重要性。

papers.title: Knowledge attitudes and practices of household heads toward rabies and associated factors in Tarcha Town, Southwest Ethiopia
papers.abstract: Rabies is a fatal zoonotic viral disease and remains a major public health challenge in developing countries, including Ethiopia. The burden is driven by limited community awareness, poor preventive practices, and inadequate access to timely post-exposure prophylaxis. Evidence on knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward rabies is limited in southwestern Ethiopia, particularly in Tarcha Town. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding rabies among household heads and to identify factors associated with KAP levels. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted from May to June 2023 among 548 household heads selected using simple random sampling. Data were collected using a pretested structured questionnaire, entered into EpiData version 3.1, and analyzed using SPSS version 26. Bivariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with KAP outcomes. Overall, 60.8% of respondents had good knowledge, 52.2% had positive attitudes, and 56.0% demonstrated good practices toward rabies prevention and control. Ownership of two or more dogs was significantly associated with good knowledge (AOR = 5.39, 95% CI 2.54–11.48, p < 0.001). Participants who could reach a veterinary clinic within 30 min had higher odds of having a positive attitude toward rabies prevention and control compared with those who required more than 30 min to reach a veterinary clinic (AOR = 3.17, 95% CI 1.14–8.86). Participants with a previous history of dog-bite exposure had higher odds of good rabies-prevention practices than participants without such a history. (AOR = 4.33, 95% CI 2.14–8.74, p < 0.001). This study found that more than half of the household heads had adequate knowledge, positive attitudes, and good practices regarding rabies. However, misconceptions and inadequate preventive practices were still observed among a considerable proportion of participants. Knowledge, attitudes, and practices were significantly associated with several socio-demographic and access-related factors. These findings indicate the need to strengthen rabies awareness and health education interventions in the study area.

elements_zh.methods: 使用预先测试的结构化问卷收集数据,输入 EpiData 3.1 版,并使用 SPSS 26 版进行分析。进行双变量和多变量逻辑回归分析,以确定与 KAP 结果相关的因素。
elements_zh.main_results: Overall, 60.8% of respondents had good knowledge, 52.2% had positive attitudes, and 56.0% demonstrated good practices toward rabies prevention and control. elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 知识、态度和实践与一些社会人口和获取相关因素显着相关。本研究发现,超过一半的户主对狂犬病有足够的了解、积极的态度和良好的做法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明需要加强研究区域的 狂犬病 意识和健康教育干预措施。这一负担是由有限的社区意识、不良的预防措施以及无法及时获取 暴露后预防 造成的。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计的具体局限性。由于该研究基于自我报告的数据和横断面设计,因此证据强度中等。

papers.title: Emerging zoonotic diseases management: designing One Health interventions through a community lens including mental health
papers.abstract: Introduction The One Health (OH) approach has emerged as a comprehensive approach that recognizes the complexity of health challenges. Previous global health emergencies including Ebola and Covid-19 caused major social and psychological disruptions, generating fear, stigma, distrust, denial of disease and resistance to control measures. This study aims to investigate stakeholder OH perspectives and to assist in designing adaptations for interventions through a community lens, including for mental health. Methods This mixed-methods study draws upon OH coordination activities and field experiences in Senegal and has been conducted between 2022 and 2024. Data sources include records of activities implemented through the National OH platform, epidemiological investigations carried out in collaboration with the Institut Pasteur de Dakar and the Ministry of Health and Social Action, and subsequent field investigations conducted in 2024. Qualitative information has been collected through participatory observation, field reports from eight OH coordination meetings, and nine semi-structured interviews conducted during the epidemiological investigations. In addition, 35 key informant interviews have been conducted with governmental, institutional, and community stakeholders involved in epidemic preparedness and response. Narrative accounts have been collected from 27 patients, survivors, and caregivers in relation to Covid-19, rabies, and Crimean Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF), as well as from four livestock keepers who had experienced animal losses. Quantitative data have been obtained through a survey of 434 livestock keepers assessing their knowledge, perceptions, and practices related to zoonotic diseases and OH interventions. Results The study has identified several indicators of psychosocial distress among affected individuals and communities. Analysis of the OH coordination platform has shown that emergency responses were primarily organized around collaboration between the human, animal, and environmental health sectors, with operational activities mainly focused on surveillance, case detection, and contact tracing. Yet, social scientists, psychologists, and social workers were rarely involved in preparedness and outbreak responses. The study also revealed limited knowledge of zoonotic diseases among livestock keepers, with the majority (89.86%) recognizing only one or two diseases. Low knowledge was significantly associated with lower levels of formal education ( p < 0.03). However, respondents demonstrated local knowledge of these diseases, describing some of them using local names. Most respondents (87.1%) reported no prior knowledge of the OH approach, while 75.81% were aware that diseases could be transmitted from animals to humans. Conclusion The study suggests that OH interventions should be designed to bridge central decision making, operational planning, and community realities by integrating local knowledge, strengthening cross-sectoral collaboration and incorporating psychosocial dimensions into epidemic preparedness and response strategies.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease, aiming to investigate stakeholder One Health perspectives and design interventions through a community lens, including mental health aspects.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This mixed-methods study draws upon One Health coordination activities and field experiences in Senegal, conducted between 2022 and 2024. Data sources include records of activities from the National OH platform, epidemiological investigations with the Institut Pasteur de Dakar and the Ministry of Health and Social Action, and field investigations in 2024. Qualitative data were collected through participatory observation, field reports from eight OH coordination meetings, and nine semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were obtained through a survey of 434 livestock keepers assessing their knowledge, perceptions, and practices related to zoonotic diseases and OH interventions.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study identified psychosocial distress indicators among affected individuals and communities. It also revealed limited knowledge of zoonotic diseases among livestock keepers, with most recognizing only one or two diseases. Low knowledge was significantly associated with lower formal education levels. Respondents showed local knowledge of these diseases, describing them using local names. Most respondents had no prior knowledge of the OH approach, but many were aware of animal-to-human disease transmission. The study concludes that OH interventions should integrate local knowledge, strengthen cross-sectoral collaboration, and incorporate psychosocial dimensions into epidemic preparedness and response strategies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study notes that social scientists, psychologists, and social workers were rarely involved in preparedness and outbreak responses. There is a gap in understanding how to effectively integrate mental health considerations into OH interventions. The evidence also highlights a need for better knowledge dissemination about zoonotic diseases and OH strategies among the general population.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The study suggests the need for more inclusive OH strategies that involve mental health professionals and community stakeholders. It emphasizes the importance of tailoring interventions to local knowledge and practices, and improving education on zoonotic diseases and OH approaches. Additionally, it highlights the need for further research on the role of psychosocial factors in outbreak responses and the development of targeted educational programs for livestock keepers.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of the One Health approach in managing rabies virus and rabies disease, emphasizing the integration of community perspectives and mental health considerations. The study, conducted in Senegal between 2022 and 2024, combines qualitative and quantitative data to assess knowledge, perceptions, and practices related to zoonotic diseases. It identifies psychosocial distress indicators and highlights limited knowledge among livestock keepers, with education levels significantly influencing awareness. The review concludes that OH interventions should incorporate local knowledge, strengthen cross-sectoral collaboration, and address mental health aspects. However, it notes the underrepresentation of social scientists in outbreak responses and calls for further research on integrating psychosocial dimensions into OH strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病,旨在调查利益相关者 One Health 的观点并通过社区视角设计干预措施,包括心理健康方面。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这项混合方法研究借鉴了 2022 年至 2024 年期间在塞内加尔开展的“同一个健康”协调活动和实地经验。数据来源包括国家 OH 平台的活动记录、达喀尔巴斯德研究所和卫生与社会行动部的流行病学调查以及 2024 年的实地调查。定性数据是通过参与性观察、八次 OH 协调会议的现场报告以及九次半结构化访谈收集的。通过对 434 名牲畜饲养者进行调查,评估他们对人畜共患疾病和职业健康干预的知识、看法和做法,获得了定量数据。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该研究确定了受影响个人和社区的社会心理困扰指标。它还揭示了牲畜饲养者对人畜共患疾病的了解有限,大多数人只认识一两种疾病。知识水平低与正规教育水平较低显着相关。受访者展示了对这些疾病的当地了解,并使用当地名称描述它们。大多数受访者事先不了解 OH 方法,但许多人都知道动物传染人类的疾病 传播。该研究的结论是,卫生干预措施应整合当地知识,加强跨部门合作,并将社会心理层面纳入流行病防范和应对策略。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究指出,社会科学家、心理学家和社会工作者很少参与准备和 暴发 应对工作。对于如何有效地将心理健康考虑因素纳入职业健康干预措施中,人们的理解存在差距。证据还强调需要在普通人群中更好地传播有关人畜共患疾病和卫生保健策略的知识。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该研究表明,需要制定更具包容性的职业健康策略,让心理健康专业人员和社区利益相关者参与进来。它强调根据当地知识和实践制定干预措施以及改进人畜共患疾病和职业健康方法教育的重要性。此外,它强调需要进一步研究心理社会因素在 暴发 反应中的作用,并为牲畜饲养者制定有针对性的教育计划。

papers.abstract_zh: 简介 One Health (OH) 方法已成为一种认识到健康挑战的复杂性的综合方法。此前发生的埃博拉和 Covid-19 等全球突发卫生事件造成了重大的社会和心理混乱,产生了恐惧、耻辱、不信任、否认疾病和抵制控制措施。本研究旨在调查利益相关者的 OH 观点,并通过社区视角协助设计干预措施,包括心理健康干预措施。方法 这项混合方法研究借鉴了塞内加尔 OH 协调活动和现场经验,于 2022 年至 2024 年之间进行。数据来源包括通过国家 OH 平台实施的活动记录、与达喀尔巴斯德研究所和卫生与社会行动部合作开展的流行病学调查以及 2024 年进行的后续实地调查。通过参与性观察和八个 OH 协调的现场报告收集了定性信息会议以及流行病学调查期间进行的九次半结构化访谈。此外,还对参与流行病防范和应对的政府、机构和社区利益相关者进行了 35 次关键知情人访谈。我们收集了 27 名与 Covid-19、狂犬病 和克里米亚刚果出血热 (CCHF) 相关的患者、幸存者和护理人员以及四名经历过动物损失的牲畜饲养者的叙述。通过对 434 名牲畜饲养者进行调查,评估他们对人畜共患疾病和职业健康干预的知识、看法和做法,获得了定量数据。结果 该研究确定了受影响个人和社区心理困扰的多项指标。对OH协调平台的分析表明,应急响应主要围绕人类、动物和环境卫生部门之间的合作进行组织,业务活动主要集中在监测、病例检测和接触者追踪等方面。然而,社会科学家、心理学家和社会工作者很少参与准备工作和 暴发 应对工作。研究还显示,牲畜饲养者对人畜共患疾病的了解有限,大多数人(89.86%)只认识一两种疾病。知识水平低与正规教育水平较低显着相关(p < 0.03)。然而,受访者展示了当地对这些疾病的了解,并使用当地名称描述了其中一些疾病。大多数受访者 (87.1%) 表示事先不了解 OH 方法,而 75.81% 的受访者知道疾病可以从动物传播给人类。结论 该研究表明,卫生干预措施的设计应通过整合当地知识、加强跨部门合作以及将心理社会维度纳入流行病防范和应对策略,在中央决策、业务规划和社区现实之间架起桥梁。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这项混合方法研究借鉴了 2022 年至 2024 年期间在塞内加尔开展的“同一个健康”协调活动和实地经验。数据来源包括国家 OH 平台的活动记录、达喀尔巴斯德研究所和卫生与社会行动部的流行病学调查以及 2024 年的实地调查。定性数据是通过参与性观察、八次 OH 协调会议的现场报告以及九次半结构化访谈收集的。通过对 434 名牲畜饲养者进行调查,评估他们对人畜共患疾病和职业健康干预的知识、看法和做法,获得了定量数据。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该研究确定了受影响个人和社区的社会心理困扰指标。它还揭示了牲畜饲养者对人畜共患疾病的了解有限,大多数人只认识一两种疾病。知识水平低与正规教育水平较低显着相关。受访者展示了对这些疾病的当地了解,并使用当地名称描述它们。大多数受访者事先不了解 OH 方法,但许多人都知道动物传染人类的疾病 传播。该研究的结论是,卫生干预措施应整合当地知识,加强跨部门合作,并将社会心理层面纳入流行病防范和应对策略。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究指出,社会科学家、心理学家和社会工作者很少参与准备和 暴发 应对工作。对于如何有效地将心理健康考虑因素纳入职业健康干预措施中,人们的理解存在差距。证据还强调需要在普通人群中更好地传播有关人畜共患疾病和卫生保健策略的知识。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该研究表明,需要制定更具包容性的职业健康策略,让心理健康专业人员和社区利益相关者参与进来。它强调根据当地知识和实践制定干预措施以及改进人畜共患疾病和职业健康方法教育的重要性。此外,它强调需要进一步研究心理社会因素在 暴发 反应中的作用,并为牲畜饲养者制定有针对性的教育计划。

papers.title: Microbiological safety assessment of canine adipose derived mesenchymal stem cell preparations reveal no detectable contamination
papers.abstract: The experimental application of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (cAD-MSC) has demonstrated excellent therapeutic potential in the treatment of a number of previously untreatable or difficult-to-treat diseases. However, the production of cAD-MSC for clinical application necessitates in vitro isolation and cell expansion, introducing the risk of microbiological contamination. Studies indicate that stored MSCs may be contaminated with bacteria, fungi, or viruses, resulting in cell transformation, cell death, or persistent infection. This ultimately compromises therapeutic efficacy and potentially facilitates therapy-induced pathogen transmission. In accordance with the European Medicines Agency guidelines mandating sterility testing as an integral component of the manufacturing process, this study aimed to assess the sterility of the cAD-MSC bank at the Croatian Veterinary Institute. To test for the most clinically significant canine pathogens, nucleic acids were extracted from 32 cAD-MSC preparations and analyzed using standard molecular PCR methods. The pathogen screening panel included rabies virus (Lyssavirus), canine herpesvirus (Varicellovirus canidalpha1), parvovirus (Carnivore protoparvovirus 1), coronavirus (Alphacoronavirus 1), distemper virus (Morbillivirus canis), Rotavirus A, Leptospira spp, Brucella canis, Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato, Anaplasma spp, Ehrlichia spp, Mycoplasma spp (hemotropic), and Neospora caninum. No tested gene fragments of the aforementioned pathogens were detected, indicating that the cAD-MSC preparations were free from the presence of clinically significant pathogens. Rigorous implementation of sterility control during the cell isolation and expansion process is essential to ensure safe cell-based therapy in canine patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the microbiological safety of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell (cAD-MSC) preparations, addressing the concern that such preparations may be contaminated with pathogens that could compromise therapeutic efficacy and pose risks to canine patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted at the Croatian Veterinary Institute, where 32 cAD-MSC preparations were tested for the presence of clinically significant pathogens, including rabies virus, as part of a sterility assessment aligned with European Medicines Agency guidelines.
analysis.methods: Nucleic acids were extracted from the 32 cAD-MSC preparations and analyzed using standard molecular PCR methods to detect the presence of specific pathogens, including rabies virus, in the preparations.
analysis.main_results: No gene fragments of rabies virus or any other tested pathogens were detected in the 32 cAD-MSC preparations, indicating that they were free from contamination with these clinically significant agents.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that the cAD-MSC preparations met sterility requirements, offering a novel confirmation of their safety for therapeutic use in canine patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical information for ensuring the safety of cell-based therapies in veterinary medicine, particularly for rabies virus, which is a significant public health concern in canine populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to testing a specific set of pathogens, and while it provides strong evidence for the absence of rabies virus, further testing may be required to confirm safety against other potential contaminants.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the microbiological safety of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell (cAD-MSC) preparations, focusing on the presence of rabies virus and other clinically significant pathogens. The research was conducted at the Croatian Veterinary Institute, where 32 cAD-MSC samples were tested using molecular PCR methods. No evidence of rabies virus or other pathogens was found, indicating that the preparations were free from contamination. The study highlights the importance of sterility testing in cell-based therapies for canine patients, particularly given the risks associated with rabies virus. While the findings support the safety of these preparations, the study's scope is limited to the tested pathogens, and further research may be necessary to ensure comprehensive safety. The evidence is strong for the absence of rabies virus but does not address other potential contaminants.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the microbiological safety of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell (cAD-MSC) preparations, addressing the concern that such preparations may be contaminated with pathogens that could compromise therapeutic efficacy and pose risks to canine patients.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted at the Croatian Veterinary Institute, where 32 cAD-MSC preparations were tested for the presence of clinically significant pathogens, including rabies virus, as part of a sterility assessment aligned with European Medicines Agency guidelines.
analysis_en.methods: Nucleic acids were extracted from the 32 cAD-MSC preparations and analyzed using standard molecular PCR methods to detect the presence of specific pathogens, including rabies virus, in the preparations.
analysis_en.main_results: No gene fragments of rabies virus or any other tested pathogens were detected in the 32 cAD-MSC preparations, indicating that they were free from contamination with these clinically significant agents.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that the cAD-MSC preparations met sterility requirements, offering a novel confirmation of their safety for therapeutic use in canine patients.

papers.title_zh: 犬脂肪间充质干细胞制剂的微生物安全评估显示没有可检测到的污染
papers.source_body_en: The experimental application of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (cAD-MSC) has demonstrated excellent therapeutic potential in the treatment of a number of previously untreatable or difficult-to-treat diseases. However, the production of cAD-MSC for clinical application necessitates in vitro isolation and cell expansion, introducing the risk of microbiological contamination. Studies indicate that stored MSCs may be contaminated with bacteria, fungi, or viruses, resulting in cell transformation, cell death, or persistent infection. This ultimately compromises therapeutic efficacy and potentially facilitates therapy-induced pathogen transmission. In accordance with the European Medicines Agency guidelines mandating sterility testing as an integral component of the manufacturing process, this study aimed to assess the sterility of the cAD-MSC bank at the Croatian Veterinary Institute. To test for the most clinically significant canine pathogens, nucleic acids were extracted from 32 cAD-MSC preparations and analyzed using standard molecular PCR methods. The pathogen screening panel included rabies virus (Lyssavirus), canine herpesvirus (Varicellovirus canidalpha1), parvovirus (Carnivore protoparvovirus 1), coronavirus (Alphacoronavirus 1), distemper virus (Morbillivirus canis), Rotavirus A, Leptospira spp, Brucella canis, Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato, Anaplasma spp, Ehrlichia spp, Mycoplasma spp (hemotropic), and Neospora caninum. No tested gene fragments of the aforementioned pathogens were detected, indicating that the cAD-MSC preparations were free from the presence of clinically significant pathogens. Rigorous implementation of sterility control during the cell isolation and expansion process is essential to ensure safe cell-based therapy in canine patients.
papers.abstract_zh: 犬脂肪源性间充质干细胞/基质细胞(cAD-MSC)的实验应用已证明治疗对许多以前无法治疗或难以治疗的疾病具有优异的治疗潜力。然而,用于临床应用的cAD-MSC的生产需要体外分离和细胞扩增,从而引入微生物污染的风险。研究表明,储存的间充质干细胞可能被细菌、真菌或病毒污染,导致细胞转化、细胞死亡或持续感染。这最终会损害治疗效果并可能促进治疗诱导的病原体 传播。根据欧洲药品管理局指南,要求将无菌检测作为生产过程的一个组成部分,本研究旨在评估克罗地亚兽医研究所 cAD-MSC 库的无菌性。为了检测临床上最重要的犬病原体,从 32 个 cAD-MSC 制剂中提取核酸,并使用标准分子 PCR 方法进行分析。病原体筛查小组包括狂犬病病毒(狂犬病毒)、犬疱疹病毒(Varicellovirus canidalpha1)、细小病毒(Carnivore protoparvovirus 1)、冠状病毒(Alphacoronavirus 1)、犬瘟热病毒(Morbillivirus canis)、轮状病毒A、钩端螺旋体属、犬布鲁氏菌、伯氏疏螺旋体、无形体spp、埃利希体属、支原体属(嗜血性)和犬新孢子虫。没有检测到上述病原体的测试基因片段,表明cAD-MSC制剂不存在临床上显着的病原体。在细胞分离和扩增过程中严格实施无菌控制对于确保犬类患者的安全细胞治疗至关重要。

papers.title: Đặc điểm dịch tễ học các trường hợp điều trị dự phòng Dại sau phơi nhiễm và một số yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận điều trị dự phòng tại thành phố Đồng Nai (địa giới hành chính trước sáp nhập) năm 2025 Epidemiological characteristics of post-exposure rabies prophylaxis cases and factors associated with the time to access prophylaxis in Dong Nai City (administrative boundaries prior to merger) in 2025
papers.abstract: Tại Đồng Nai (địa giới hành chính trước sáp nhập), giai đoạn 2023–2025 ghi nhận 10 người tử vong dobệnh Dại, 117 ổ dịch trên động vật và số người điều trị dự phòng Dại sau phơi nhiễm (RPEP) tăng hơn1,5 lần mỗi năm. Mục tiêu của nghiên cứu này nhằm mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ học các trường hợp RPEP vàmột số yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận RPEP tại thành phố Đồng Nai năm 2025. Thiết kế nghiêncứu mô tả, hồi cứu toàn bộ dữ liệu của 37.976 trường hợp RPEP từ 64 điểm tiêm phòng Dại. Phân tíchhồi quy đa biến được sử dụng để xác định yếu tố liên quan đến tiếp cận RPEP muộn (được định nghĩalà bắt đầu tiêm phòng ≥2 ngày sau phơi nhiễm). Trong 37.976 người RPEP; 53,7% là nam giới và 33,4%là nhóm tuổi 25–49. Số người bị phơi nhiễm vào cuối tuần chiếm 31,2%; 19,8% bị mèo cào/cắn; 2,9% bịvết thương đầu–mặt–cổ và 11,4% phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường. Tỷ lệ tiếp cận RPEPmuộn là 23,3%. Các yếu tố liên quan đến tiếp cận RPEP muộn gồm: bị cắn vào cuối tuần (aOR=1,9; 95%CI: 1,77–2,01); phơi nhiễm do mèo (aOR=1,3; 95% CI: 1,25–1,40); phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiệnbất thường (aOR=1,7; 95% CI: 1,62–1,88), vết cắn vùng đầu–mặt–cổ (aOR=1,5; 95% CI: 1,34–1,73). Đểcải thiện thời gian tiếp cận RPEP, cần truyền thông nguy cơ đối với các trường hợp phơi nhiễm từ độngvật biểu hiện bất thường, vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ, phơi nhiễm do mèo và công khai địa chỉ, thời gianhoạt động cuối tuần của các điểm tiêm Dại.
papers.journal: Tạp chí Y học Dự phòng

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nghiên cứu này được thực hiện để mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ học của các trường hợp điều trị dự phòng dại sau phơi nhiễm và các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến thời gian tiếp cận điều trị. Tại Đồng Nai, giai đoạn 2023–2025 ghi nhận 10 ca tử vong do dại, 117 ổ dịch trên động vật và số ca điều trị dự phòng dại sau phơi nhiễm (RPEP) tăng hơn 1,5 lần mỗi năm.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Nghiên cứu mô tả, hồi cứu toàn bộ dữ liệu của 37.976 trường hợp RPEP từ 64 điểm tiêm phòng dại tại Đồng Nai trong năm 2025. Nghiên cứu tập trung vào các yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận RPEP, bao gồm cả các ca phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường.
analysis.methods: Phân tích hồi quy đa biến được sử dụng để xác định các yếu tố liên quan đến việc tiếp cận RPEP muộn, được định nghĩa là bắt đầu tiêm phòng ≥2 ngày sau phơi nhiễm. Các yếu tố được xem xét bao gồm thời gian phơi nhiễm, loại động vật gây thương tích và thời gian tiếp cận dịch vụ tiêm phòng.
analysis.main_results: Trong 37.976 trường hợp RPEP, 53,7% là nam giới và 33,4% thuộc nhóm tuổi 25–49. 31,2% các ca phơi nhiễm xảy ra vào cuối tuần, 19,8% bị mèo cào/cắn, 2,9% bị vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ và 11,4% phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường. Tỷ lệ tiếp cận RPEP muộn là 23,3%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Kết quả cho thấy các yếu tố như phơi nhiễm vào cuối tuần, do mèo gây ra, từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường và vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ có liên quan đến việc tiếp cận RPEP muộn. Đây là thông tin mới về các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến thời gian tiêm phòng dại tại Đồng Nai.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Kết quả nghiên cứu có thể hỗ trợ cải thiện chiến lược truyền thông và phân bổ dịch vụ tiêm phòng dại, đặc biệt là đối với các ca phơi nhiễm từ động vật bất thường, vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ và vào cuối tuần.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Nghiên cứu dựa trên dữ liệu hồi cứu, có thể tồn tại sai sót trong việc ghi chép. Tuy nhiên, các kết quả được hỗ trợ bởi phân tích hồi quy đa biến, cho thấy mức độ tin cậy cao trong việc xác định các yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận RPEP.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to describe the epidemiological characteristics of post-exposure rabies prophylaxis (RPEP) cases and factors associated with delayed access to RPEP in Dong Nai City in 2025. It analyzed data from 37,976 RPEP cases across 64 vaccination sites. The main results indicated that 53.7% of cases were male, 33.4% were aged 25–49, and 31.2% occurred on weekends. Factors linked to delayed RPEP access included weekend exposure (aOR=1.9; 95% CI: 1.77–2.01), cat bites (aOR=1.3; 95% CI: 1.25–1.40), exposure to animals with abnormal behavior (aOR=1.7; 95% CI: 1.62–1.88), and head–face–neck injuries (aOR=1.5; 95% CI: 1.34–1.73). The study highlights the need for targeted communication and improved access to rabies prophylaxis services, particularly for high-risk groups. The evidence is strong, supported by multivariate regression analysis, but the study design is limited to retrospective data collection.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Nghiên cứu này được thực hiện để mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ học của các trường hợp điều trị dự phòng dại sau phơi nhiễm và các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến thời gian tiếp cận điều trị. Tại Đồng Nai, giai đoạn 2023–2025 ghi nhận 10 ca tử vong do dại, 117 ổ dịch trên động vật và số ca điều trị dự phòng dại sau phơi nhiễm (RPEP) tăng hơn 1,5 lần mỗi năm.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: Nghiên cứu mô tả, hồi cứu toàn bộ dữ liệu của 37.976 trường hợp RPEP từ 64 điểm tiêm phòng dại tại Đồng Nai trong năm 2025. Nghiên cứu tập trung vào các yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận RPEP, bao gồm cả các ca phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường.
elements_en.methods: Phân tích hồi quy đa biến được sử dụng để xác định các yếu tố liên quan đến việc tiếp cận RPEP muộn, được định nghĩa là bắt đầu tiêm phòng ≥2 ngày sau phơi nhiễm. Các yếu tố được xem xét bao gồm thời gian phơi nhiễm, loại động vật gây thương tích và thời gian tiếp cận dịch vụ tiêm phòng.
elements_en.main_results: Trong 37.976 trường hợp RPEP, 53,7% là nam giới và 33,4% thuộc nhóm tuổi 25–49. 31,2% các ca phơi nhiễm xảy ra vào cuối tuần, 19,8% bị mèo cào/cắn, 2,9% bị vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ và 11,4% phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường. Tỷ lệ tiếp cận RPEP muộn là 23,3%.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Kết quả cho thấy các yếu tố như phơi nhiễm vào cuối tuần, do mèo gây ra, từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường và vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ có liên quan đến việc tiếp cận RPEP muộn. Đây là thông tin mới về các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến thời gian tiêm phòng dại tại Đồng Nai.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Kết quả nghiên cứu có thể hỗ trợ cải thiện chiến lược truyền thông và phân bổ dịch vụ tiêm phòng dại, đặc biệt là đối với các ca phơi nhiễm từ động vật bất thường, vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ và vào cuối tuần.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Nghiên cứu dựa trên dữ liệu hồi cứu, có thể tồn tại sai sót trong việc ghi chép. Tuy nhiên, các kết quả được hỗ trợ bởi phân tích hồi quy đa biến, cho thấy mức độ tin cậy cao trong việc xác định các yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận RPEP.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: Nghiên cứu này được thực hiện để mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ học của các trường hợp điều trị dự phòng dại sau phơi nhiễm và các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến thời gian tiếp cận điều trị. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 描述性研究回顾了2025年同奈省64个狂犬病疫苗接种点的37.976例暴露后预防病例数据,研究重点包括接触狂犬病暴露后预防的时间因素,包括来自有异常表现动物的暴露病例。
elements_zh.methods: 采用多变量回归分析以确定导致RPEP治疗延迟的相关因素,定义为暴露后≥2天开始接种。分析因素包括暴露时间、致伤动物类型以及接种服务的获取时间。
elements_zh.main_results: Trong 37.976 trường hợp RPEP, 53,7% là nam giới và 33,4% thuộc nhóm tuổi 25–49. 31,2% các ca phơi nhiễm xảy ra vào cuối tuần, 19,8% bị mèo cào/cắn, 2,9% bị vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ và 11,4% phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường. Tỷ lệ tiếp cận RPEP muộn là 23,3%.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,周末暴露、猫源性暴露、暴露于有异常行为的动物以及头部、面部、颈部伤口等因素与RPEP治疗延迟相关。这是关于影响同奈市狂犬病暴露后预防治疗及时性的新信息。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究结果可为改善狂犬病暴露后预防的宣传策略和疫苗接种服务的分配提供依据,特别是针对暴露于异常动物、头部、面部、颈部伤口以及周末暴露的病例。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于回顾性数据,可能存在记录误差。然而,多变量回归分析的结果表明,确定影响RPEP治疗及时性的相关因素具有较高的可信度。

papers.title_zh: dặc điểm dịch tễ học các trường hợp điều trị dự phòng Dại sau phơi nhiễm và một số yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận điều trị dự phòng tại thành phố Đồng Nai (địa giới hành chính trước sáp nhập) năm 2025 2025年同奈市(合并前的行政边界)暴露后狂犬病预防病例的流行病学特征以及与获得预防治疗时间相关的因素
papers.source_body_en: Tại Đồng Nai (địa giới hành chính trước sáp nhập), giai đoạn 2023–2025 ghi nhận 10 người tử vong dobệnh Dại, 117 ổ dịch trên động vật và số người điều trị dự phòng Dại sau phơi nhiễm (RPEP) tăng hơn1,5 lần mỗi năm. Mục tiêu của nghiên cứu này nhằm mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ học các trường hợp RPEP vàmột số yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận RPEP tại thành phố Đồng Nai năm 2025. Thiết kế nghiêncứu mô tả, hồi cứu toàn bộ dữ liệu của 37.976 trường hợp RPEP từ 64 điểm tiêm phòng Dại. Phân tíchhồi quy đa biến được sử dụng để xác định yếu tố liên quan đến tiếp cận RPEP muộn (được định nghĩalà bắt đầu tiêm phòng ≥2 ngày sau phơi nhiễm). Trong 37.976 người RPEP; 53,7% là nam giới và 33,4%là nhóm tuổi 25–49. Số người bị phơi nhiễm vào cuối tuần chiếm 31,2%; 19,8% bị mèo cào/cắn; 2,9% bịvết thương đầu–mặt–cổ và 11,4% phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường. Tỷ lệ tiếp cận RPEPmuộn là 23,3%. Các yếu tố liên quan đến tiếp cận RPEP muộn gồm: bị cắn vào cuối tuần (aOR=1,9; 95%CI: 1,77–2,01); phơi nhiễm do mèo (aOR=1,3; 95% CI: 1,25–1,40); phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiệnbất thường (aOR=1,7; 95% CI: 1,62–1,88), vết cắn vùng đầu–mặt–cổ (aOR=1,5; 95% CI: 1,34–1,73). Đểcải thiện thời gian tiếp cận RPEP, cần truyền thông nguy cơ đối với các trường hợp phơi nhiễm từ độngvật biểu hiện bất thường, vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ, phơi nhiễm do mèo và công khai địa chỉ, thời gianhoạt động cuối tuần của các điểm tiêm Dại.

papers.title: Editorial: Measuring vaccination perception, confidence, and uptake: advancing instrument development and validation
papers.abstract: Two contributions in this Research Topic directly advance the measurement science that motivated this Topic. ground the development of a new general measure of adult vaccine hesitancy for U.S. adults in the 3C framework, reporting content and face validity findings, including a content validity index derived from expert panel review, for an instrument intended to capture hesitancy across vaccine types rather than a single indication. report the development and psychometric evaluation of the Vaccine Hesitancy and Perception Scale toward COVID-19 vaccination (VHAPS-CV19), employing principal axis factoring with varimax rotation to derive a two-factor structure that distinguishes a hesitancy factor (confidence, complacency, and convenience) from a perception-and-trust factor (perceived benefit, barrier, susceptibility, severity, and trust), together with internal consistency estimates for each subscale. Together, the two studies trace the stages that valid measurement of a construct this complex demands, from item generation and content validity through factor structure and reliability testing, and they leave the field with two complementary tools, one general-purpose and one vaccine-specific, for future validation and cross-cultural adaptation work.Several contributions in this Topic examine hesitancy and uptake among healthcare workers, a population whose own vaccination behavior and patient communication directly shape public confidence. investigated uptake, willingness, and practices toward seasonal influenza vaccination among healthcare workers in China using a cross-sectional design. similarly employed a cross-sectional survey to explore attitudes toward COVID-19 vaccination among healthcare workers at a national infectious disease center in Singapore, while Aksoy et al. surveyed community pharmacists in Türkiye regarding their knowledge, attitudes, and barriers toward vaccination, extending the focus to frontline advocates outside the hospital setting. took a distinct, qualitative approach, interviewing healthcare workers at a London hospital to identify barriers and facilitators to measles vaccination uptake; this design complements the quantitative work elsewhere in the Topic, surfacing workplace, informational, and interpersonal factors that structured surveys tend to miss.A second cluster of contributions addresses hesitancy and uptake determinants in community and general-population samples, extending the scope of this Topic beyond influenza and COVID-19 to additional vaccine types and life stages. Rounding out the collection, Ali et al. provide a narrative review of enablers and barriers to influenza vaccine uptake among healthcare workers in Gulf Cooperation Council countries, synthesizing evidence from a regional context that is comparatively underrepresented in the vaccine hesitancy literature relative to North America, Europe, and East Asia. contribute a distinct but complementary perspective, presenting a multivariate analysis of risk factors for adverse events following rabies vaccination using real-world data. This work centers on vaccine safety rather than perception, but it is a reminder that confidence in vaccination rests on lived experience with tolerability as much as on attitudes and access, and that perception-focused instruments are best read alongside pharmacovigilance data.A few patterns stand out across this collection (Figure 1; Table 1). Geographically, contributions concentrate in China (six studies), with additional representation from the United States, Singapore, Türkiye, Vietnam, the United Kingdom, and the Gulf Cooperation Council region; populations in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America are absent, which limits how far these findings generalize and points to a direction for future Research Topics. Methodologically, most contributions rely on cross-sectional, self-report surveys. These designs are useful for generating hypotheses about correlates of hesitancy, but they cannot establish temporal precedence between attitude and behavior, and they remain vulnerable to social desirability and recall bias. Only one contribution employed qualitative interview methods, and none employed a longitudinal or experimental design; this concentration of designs mirrors the broader hesitancy literature and marks a gap that future work should close.Taken together, the contributions to this Research Topic make clear that vaccine decision-making has many layers. Hesitancy and confidence are shaped at once by individual psychology, professional role, cultural context, service accessibility, and direct experience with vaccine safety. The instrument development studies respond to a real methodological gap: the field needs measurement tools that are psychometrically sound and adaptable across populations. The determinant studies argue the opposite case for context. Findings from healthcare workers in the Gulf region, older adults in western China, and pharmacists in Türkiye are not interchangeable; each offers insight for the setting studied rather than a universal account of vaccine hesitancy.A few gaps remain for future research. Cross-cultural validation of the instruments introduced here, including measurement invariance testing and comparison against benchmarks such as the WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Scale (2), would strengthen confidence in their applicability across populations. Longitudinal designs tracking how measured hesitancy or confidence relates to actual vaccination behavior over time, rather than to intention alone, would help close the well-documented gap between attitudinal measurement and uptake outcomes. Greater use of qualitative and mixed-methods designs, alongside the cross-sectional surveys predominant here, would help clarify mechanisms that quantitative models identify but cannot fully explain. Finally, as vaccine platforms and communication environments evolve, measurement tools will need periodic re-validation to remain sensitive to emerging determinants of hesitancy.

papers.title_original: Editorial: Measuring vaccination perception, confidence, and uptake: advancing instrument development and validation

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease. It examines the measurement of vaccination perception, confidence, and uptake, particularly among healthcare workers and general populations, with an emphasis on developing psychometrically sound instruments for assessing vaccine hesitancy across different contexts.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is an editorial that compiles contributions from various studies. These studies primarily use cross-sectional, self-report surveys to investigate vaccine hesitancy and uptake. A few studies employ qualitative interview methods, while none use longitudinal or experimental designs. The review does not explicitly report a meta-analysis or consensus process but synthesizes findings from multiple studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that vaccine decision-making involves multiple factors, including individual psychology, professional role, cultural context, service accessibility, and direct experience with vaccine safety. It emphasizes the need for measurement tools that are psychometrically sound and adaptable across populations, as well as the importance of cross-cultural validation and comparison against established scales like the WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Scale.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies methodological limitations, such as the inability of cross-sectional designs to establish temporal precedence between attitude and behavior, and their vulnerability to social desirability and recall bias. It also notes that findings from different populations (e.g., healthcare workers in the Gulf region, older adults in western China, and pharmacists in Türkiye) are not interchangeable, indicating a lack of generalizability. Additionally, the review points out the absence of studies in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America, which limits the scope of the findings.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on cross-cultural validation of the instruments introduced, including measurement invariance testing and benchmarking against existing scales. It also recommends the use of longitudinal designs to better understand how measured hesitancy or confidence relates to actual vaccination behavior over time. Furthermore, it highlights the need for periodic re-validation of measurement tools as vaccine platforms and communication environments evolve.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial reviews contributions to a Research Topic on measuring vaccination perception, confidence, and uptake, with a focus on rabies virus and rabies disease. It highlights the development of psychometrically sound instruments for assessing vaccine hesitancy, particularly among healthcare workers and general populations. The review identifies methodological limitations, such as the reliance on cross-sectional surveys and the absence of studies in certain regions. It emphasizes the need for cross-cultural validation, longitudinal designs, and periodic re-validation of measurement tools to improve their applicability and accuracy. The findings suggest that vaccine decision-making is influenced by multiple factors, including individual psychology, professional role, cultural context, and direct experience with vaccine safety.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病。它研究了 疫苗 感知、信心和吸收的测量,特别是在医护人员和普通人群中,重点是开发心理测量学上合理的工具来评估不同背景下的 疫苗 犹豫度。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是一篇社论,汇集了各种研究的贡献。这些研究主要使用横断面、自我报告调查来调查 疫苗 的犹豫和接受情况。一些研究采用定性访谈方法,但没有使用纵向或实验设计。该综述没有明确报告荟萃分析或共识过程,而是综合了多项研究的结果。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查强调,疫苗 决策涉及多种因素,包括个人心理、专业角色、文化背景、服务可及性以及对 疫苗 安全的直接体验。它强调需要心理测量上合理且适用于不同人群的测量工具,以及跨文化验证和与 WHO SAGE 疫苗 犹豫量表等既定量表进行比较的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出了方法上的局限性,例如横断面设计无法在态度和行为之间建立时间优先级,以及它们容易受到社会期望和回忆偏差的影响。它还指出,不同人群(例如海湾地区的医护人员、中国西部的老年人和土耳其的药剂师)的研究结果不可互换,表明缺乏普遍性。此外,审查还指出,撒哈拉以南非洲、南亚和拉丁美洲缺乏研究,这限制了研究结果的范围。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查建议未来的研究应侧重于所引入工具的跨文化验证,包括测量不变性测试和针对现有量表的基准测试。它还建议使用纵向设计来更好地了解测量的犹豫或置信度与实际 疫苗接种 行为随时间的关系。此外,它还强调了随着 疫苗 平台和通信环境的发展,需要定期重新验证测量工具。

Together, the two studies trace the stages that valid measurement of a construct this complex demands, from item generation and content validity through factor structure and reliability testing, and they leave the field with two complementary tools, one general-purpose and one vaccine-specific, for future validation and cross-cultural adaptation work.Several contributions in this Topic examine hesitancy and uptake among healthcare workers, a population whose own vaccination behavior and patient communication directly shape public confidence. investigated uptake, willingness, and practices toward seasonal influenza vaccination among healthcare workers in China using a cross-sectional design. similarly employed a cross-sectional survey to explore attitudes toward COVID-19 vaccination among healthcare workers at a national infectious disease center in Singapore, while Aksoy et al. surveyed community pharmacists in Türkiye regarding their knowledge, attitudes, and barriers toward vaccination, extending the focus to frontline advocates outside the hospital setting. took a distinct, qualitative approach, interviewing healthcare workers at a London hospital to identify barriers and facilitators to measles vaccination uptake; this design complements the quantitative work elsewhere in the Topic, surfacing workplace, informational, and interpersonal factors that structured surveys tend to miss.A second cluster of contributions addresses hesitancy and uptake determinants in community and general-population samples, extending the scope of this Topic beyond influenza and COVID-19 to additional vaccine types and life stages. Rounding out the collection, Ali et al. provide a narrative review of enablers and barriers to influenza vaccine uptake among healthcare workers in Gulf Cooperation Council countries, synthesizing evidence from a regional context that is comparatively underrepresented in the vaccine hesitancy literature relative to North America, Europe, and East Asia. contribute a distinct but complementary perspective, presenting a multivariate analysis of risk factors for adverse events following rabies vaccination using real-world data. This work centers on vaccine safety rather than perception, but it is a reminder that confidence in vaccination rests on lived experience with tolerability as much as on attitudes and access, and that perception-focused instruments are best read alongside pharmacovigilance data.A few patterns stand out across this collection (Figure 1; Table 1). Geographically, contributions concentrate in China (six studies), with additional representation from the United States, Singapore, Türkiye, Vietnam, the United Kingdom, and the Gulf Cooperation Council region; populations in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America are absent, which limits how far these findings generalize and points to a direction for future Research Topics. Methodologically, most contributions rely on cross-sectional, self-report surveys. These designs are useful for generating hypotheses about correlates of hesitancy, but they cannot establish temporal precedence between attitude and behavior, and they remain vulnerable to social desirability and recall bias. Only one contribution employed qualitative interview methods, and none employed a longitudinal or experimental design; this concentration of designs mirrors the broader hesitancy literature and marks a gap that future work should close.Taken together, the contributions to this Research Topic make clear that vaccine decision-making has many layers. Hesitancy and confidence are shaped at once by individual psychology, professional role, cultural context, service accessibility, and direct experience with vaccine safety. The instrument development studies respond to a real methodological gap: the field needs measurement tools that are psychometrically sound and adaptable across populations. The determinant studies argue the opposite case for context. Findings from healthcare workers in the Gulf region, older adults in western China, and pharmacists in Türkiye are not interchangeable; each offers insight for the setting studied rather than a universal account of vaccine hesitancy.A few gaps remain for future research. Cross-cultural validation of the instruments introduced here, including measurement invariance testing and comparison against benchmarks such as the WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Scale (2), would strengthen confidence in their applicability across populations. Longitudinal designs tracking how measured hesitancy or confidence relates to actual vaccination behavior over time, rather than to intention alone, would help close the well-documented gap between attitudinal measurement and uptake outcomes. Greater use of qualitative and mixed-methods designs, alongside the cross-sectional surveys predominant here, would help clarify mechanisms that quantitative models identify but cannot fully explain. Finally, as vaccine platforms and communication environments evolve, measurement tools will need periodic re-validation to remain sensitive to emerging determinants of hesitancy.
papers.abstract_zh: 本研究主题中的两项贡献直接推进了推动本主题的测量科学。为在 3C 框架中制定针对美国成年人的成人 疫苗 犹豫的新通用衡量标准奠定基础,报告内容和表面有效性调查结果,包括来自专家小组审查的内容有效性指数,旨在捕获跨 疫苗 类型而不是单一指标的犹豫。报告针对 COVID-19 疫苗接种 (VHAPS-CV19) 的 疫苗 犹豫和感知量表 (VHAPS-CV19) 的开发和心理测量评估,采用带有最大方差旋转的主轴因子分解来导出双因素结构,区分犹豫因素(信心、自满和便利)与感知和信任因素(感知利益、障碍、敏感性、严重性和信任),以及每个分量表的内部一致性估计。这两项研究共同追踪了有效测量这种复杂结构所需的各个阶段,从项目生成和内容有效性到因子结构和可靠性测试,并为该领域留下了两种补充工具,一种是通用的,一种是 疫苗 专用的,用于未来的验证和跨文化适应工作。本主题中的一些贡献考察了医疗保健工作者的犹豫和接受情况,他们自己的 疫苗 行为和患者沟通直接塑造了公众的信心。采用横断面设计调查了中国医护人员对季节性流感 疫苗接种 的吸收、意愿和实践。同样,他们采用了一项横断面调查来探讨新加坡国家传染病中心医护人员对 COVID-19 疫苗接种 的态度,而 Aksoy 等人。对土耳其的社区药剂师进行了调查,了解他们对 疫苗接种 的知识、态度和障碍,并将重点扩大到医院以外的一线倡导者。采用独特的定性方法,采访了伦敦一家医院的医护人员,以确定麻疹 疫苗接种 吸收的障碍和促进因素;这一设计补充了该主题其他地方的定量工作,揭示了结构化调查往往会忽略的工作场所、信息和人际因素。第二组贡献解决了社区和一般人群样本中的犹豫和吸收决定因素,将该主题的范围扩展到流感和 COVID-19 之外,扩展到其他 疫苗 类型和生命阶段。阿里等人完善了该系列。对海湾合作委员会国家医护人员中流感 疫苗 摄取的促进因素和障碍进行叙述性回顾,综合来自相对于北美、欧洲和东亚的 疫苗 犹豫文献中代表性相对不足的区域背景的证据。贡献了独特但互补的观点,使用真实世界数据对 狂犬病 疫苗接种 后不良事件的风险因素进行了多变量分析。这项工作的重点是 疫苗 的安全性而不是感知,但它提醒人们,对 疫苗 的信心不仅取决于态度和可及性,还取决于生活经验的耐受性,并且以感知为中心的工具最好与药物警戒数据一起阅读。该集合中有一些突出的模式(图 1;表 1)。从地域上看,贡献集中在中国(六项研究),其他代表来自美国、新加坡、土耳其、越南、英国和海湾合作委员会地区;撒哈拉以南非洲、南亚和拉丁美洲的人口不存在,这限制了这些发现的推广程度,并为未来的研究主题指明了方向。从方法上来说,大多数贡献都依赖于横截面的自我报告调查。这些设计对于生成有关犹豫相关性的假设很有用,但它们无法在态度和行为之间建立时间优先级,并且它们仍然容易受到社会期望和回忆偏差的影响。只有一篇文章采用了定性访谈方法,没有一篇文章采用了纵向或实验设计;这种集中的设计反映了更广泛的犹豫文献,并标志着未来工作应该弥合的差距。总而言之,对该研究主题的贡献清楚地表明,疫苗 决策具有多个层次。犹豫和信心是由个人心理、专业角色、文化背景、服务可及性以及对 疫苗 安全的直接体验决定的。仪器开发研究回应了真正的方法论差距:该领域需要心理测量上合理且适用于不同人群的测量工具。决定因素研究提出了相反的背景情况。海湾地区医护人员、中国西部老年人和土耳其药剂师的研究结果不可互换;每个都提供了对所研究环境的见解,而不是对 疫苗 犹豫的普遍解释。未来的研究仍然存在一些空白。这里介绍的工具的跨文化验证,包括测量不变性测试以及与 WHO SAGE 疫苗 犹豫量表 (2) 等基准的比较,将增强对其在人群中适用性的信心。纵向设计跟踪测量的犹豫或信心如何与实际的 疫苗接种 行为随时间的变化而不仅仅是意图相关,将有助于缩小态度测量和吸收结果之间有据可查的差距。更多地使用定性和混合方法设计,以及这里占主导地位的横截面调查,将有助于澄清定量模型识别但无法完全解释的机制。最后,随着 疫苗 平台和通信环境的发展,测量工具将需要定期重新验证,以保持对新出现的犹豫决定因素的敏感度。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病。它研究了 疫苗 感知、信心和吸收的测量,特别是在医护人员和普通人群中,重点是开发心理测量学上合理的工具来评估不同背景下的 疫苗 犹豫度。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是一篇社论,汇集了各种研究的贡献。这些研究主要使用横断面、自我报告调查来调查 疫苗 的犹豫和接受情况。一些研究采用定性访谈方法,但没有使用纵向或实验设计。该综述没有明确报告荟萃分析或共识过程,而是综合了多项研究的结果。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查强调,疫苗 决策涉及多种因素,包括个人心理、专业角色、文化背景、服务可及性以及对 疫苗 安全的直接体验。它强调需要心理测量上合理且适用于不同人群的测量工具,以及跨文化验证和与 WHO SAGE 疫苗 犹豫量表等既定量表进行比较的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出了方法上的局限性,例如横断面设计无法在态度和行为之间建立时间优先级,以及它们容易受到社会期望和回忆偏差的影响。它还指出,不同人群(例如海湾地区的医护人员、中国西部的老年人和土耳其的药剂师)的研究结果不可互换,表明缺乏普遍性。此外,审查还指出,撒哈拉以南非洲、南亚和拉丁美洲缺乏研究,这限制了研究结果的范围。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查建议未来的研究应侧重于所引入工具的跨文化验证,包括测量不变性测试和针对现有量表的基准测试。它还建议使用纵向设计来更好地了解测量的犹豫或置信度与实际 疫苗接种 行为随时间的关系。此外,它还强调了随着 疫苗 平台和通信环境的发展,需要定期重新验证测量工具。

papers.title: mRNA-based therapies: From molecular discovery to clinical revolution

source_records.title: mRNA-based therapies: From molecular discovery to clinical revolution
mRNA-based therapies: From molecular discovery to clinical revolution
